advisory.finding: Neither alarm wraps the sparse AWS/Bedrock series in FILL(...,0), unlike the sibling Bedrock alarm. If prompt caching stops entirely, CacheReadInputTokenCount publishes no datapoint, and `cache / inp` (or `cache*rate` in the cost math) has nothing to combine with. The expression then yields no value for that hour and treat_missing_data=notBreaching keeps the alarm OK. So the exact regression these alarms exist for (full cache loss, about 2x cost) can never fire either alarm.
merged_from: The two alarms read InputTokenCount in incompatible ways. The cost math prices `inp` at the uncached-input rate and adds cache reads separately, which only makes sense if InputTokenCount excludes cache reads. The ratio alarm computes `cache / inp` and describes it as a ratio 'below 80%', which only makes sense if InputTokenCount is total input. One of them is wrong. Either the ratio can exceed 1, so the 0.8 threshold means a cached share of about 44%, not 80%, or the cost estimate double-counts cached tokens.
scenarios: A model config or fallback-chain change drops cache_control: InputTokenCount spikes, CacheReadInputTokenCount goes absent, the ratio expression emits nothing, and the alarm stays OK.
The same absence removes the unit-cost datapoint exactly when cost per invocation doubles.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `IF(FILL(inp,0) > 1000000, FILL(cache,0) / inp, 1)` for the ratio and `IF(FILL(inv,0) > 5, (FILL(inp,0)*rate + FILL(cache,0)*rate + FILL(out,0)*rate)/1000000/inv, 0)` for unit cost.

advisory.finding: The notBreaching opt-out treats 'no data' as 'idle model'. But a model id that no longer receives traffic produces exactly the same absence: that is the stale 4.x-id bug this change fixes. Nothing proves these alarms are watching live series. Other opt-outs in the repo rely on a dead-man alarm for liveness; these have none. The next model cutover will leave them permanently and silently OK again.
scenarios: Production moves to a 6.x inference profile and REBAR_LLM_*_MODEL changes, but this locals map does not. Both alarms report OK forever, which reproduces bug graceless-thievish-olm.

advisory.finding: The target SNS topic bedrock-spend-cap-alerts has a custom aws_sns_topic_policy that replaces the default policy. That policy grants SNS:Publish only to the account root principal, budgets.amazonaws.com and costalerts.amazonaws.com. Nothing grants cloudwatch.amazonaws.com, so publishes from these new alarm_actions/ok_actions may be denied at the topic. The alarm would still enter ALARM state, but no notification would be sent.
merged_from: The metric-math expressions use the raw Bedrock series without FILL. If any series has no datapoint in a period, metric math drops that timestamp, the alarm treats it as missing data, and treat_missing_data = notBreaching turns that into OK. That happens in exactly the regression the alarm targets: if cache reads drop to zero, CacheReadInputTokenCount may publish nothing, so `cache / inp` and the `cache*rate` term in cpi produce no value, and neither alarm can fire.
scenarios: A prompt-caching regression drives the ratio below 80% for 3h. The alarm changes to ALARM, but the SNS publish is denied and the alarm history shows a failed action, so no one is notified.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a statement to aws_sns_topic_policy.bedrock_spend_cap_alerts: { Sid = "AllowCloudWatchAlarmsPublish", Effect = "Allow", Principal = { Service = "cloudwatch.amazonaws.com" }, Action = "SNS:Publish", Resource = aws_sns_topic.bedrock_spend_cap_alerts.arn, Condition = { StringEquals = { "aws:SourceAccount" = local.bedrock_cap_account_id } } }. After applying, use set-alarm-state on one alarm to confirm the message arrives.

advisory.finding: No regression test stops the defect this change fixes from coming back. Nothing checks that the ModelId values in `local.bedrock_cost_models` match the models production actually calls (REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL / REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL in infra/compose/docker-compose.yml). If the deployed model moves again and this map is not updated, the alarms go silent, exactly like the hand-made 4.x alarms did, and every existing test stays green.
scenarios: A later change sets REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL to "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-6-0" in docker-compose.yml but leaves `sonnet.model_id = "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5"`. Both sonnet cost alarms then watch a ModelId with no traffic, stay OK forever because of notBreaching, and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py (or a sibling test), read infra/compose/docker-compose.yml and pull out the REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL and REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL values, removing the `bedrock:` prefix. Use a regex on the masked/raw text of monitoring_bedrock_cost.tf to collect its `model_id = "..."` values. Assert both sets are non-empty (anti-vacuity), then assert the compose ids equal the Terraform ids.
